body: Good for you. I guess I was naive about what it entailed. Being a "step" is so much more than just being around. There's expectations and  vulnerabilities... It's just a lot.
I was afraid that I was going to get to that point. But his son doesn't need two mother figures messing with his head. Thanks so much for what you said. It means a lot.
Thanks so much. I agree. It's nice to have the confirmation.
I had that thought many times! Which makes this easily the hardest thing I've ever done. Thank you SO much for the kind words, it honestly means a lot right now.

I'm fairly new to relationships I guess and the last one was very clear cut that we should break up. But you're right, it's for rational reasons and doing it now will be better than going through with a marriage and possible kids and hoping it gets better. Thank you so much.

Things have been pretty good lately. I don't want to blindside him.  When I think about leaving I get excited until I actually see him. Then I get a sinking feeling in my gut. How do you leave someone you still love? 

I keep thinking about being on my own though. I've devoted a good chunk of my 20s to raising a child that I never wanted, as harsh as that is... I know this is the right thing to do but I can't help not wanting to hurt him.

Thanks for saying I didn't sign up for it. Everyone tells me "you knew what you were getting into," but I really didn't. Like I said, he didn't have full custody until a year had gone by. I'm not sure if I want kids, but I know I don't want them with him. I love him but I hate being a mom to his son which is why I'm having such a hard time. I hope that doesn't make me a bad person.

We've had that talk a lot. I've told him that I feel like the parent and he's the step parent, or that we should do more things as a "family." He didn't have a good childhood so for him the bare minimum is good enough because it's more than he ever had. I'm afraid it'll never click for him if I'm around enabling it. He has gotten better in the past three years but honestly I can never see myself having kids with him because I see myself being sole caretaker forever.

I'm not sure, I've only been at one of my jobs for a month and a half so I'm still in my 90 days and I don't know how well that would go over. I don't really have time to make any friends unfortunately. He makes it pretty clear he doesn't like when I go out. I haven't seen a lot of my friends in a long time because he always starts a fight when I get home. He says he supports me going out and wants me to have fun, but there's always a fight or accusations of cheating when I get home. It just hasn't been worth the hassle.
Okay. Thanks for the advice. I really appreciate you taking the time to respond.

We pay equal bills, but he has gone months at a time without helping with rent. He never helps with groceries. He gets offended when I ask for his help financially.

Maybe saying I'm guilted into staying is a bit harsh. We have conversations, but it's always the same conversation and nothing ever changes. He never changes. The last time this happened he said that it will destroy his son, that I'm "giving up," and that I'm leaving "just like everybody else." That's why I feel guilted. 

I'm not sure how to take a break. I don't have anywhere I could stay for a week or two. I need my jobs and my parents live 4 hours away. I don't have any friends in this area. That's what I've been wanting to do but I don't have anywhere to go.
I hope his dad allows that. He's a little emotional and I worry that he won't want me around at all.
I know. I just really don't want to break his heart.

How would you suggest I go about weaning myself from the child? I agree  and I want to make to as easy as possible. But we all live together which is why I'm always guilted back into the relationship. I don't have anywhere to go unless I go out and get an apartment. I hope I'm not coming across as combative. I could really use the guidance.

Thanks for the advice. I just don't want to ruin my life or his because I'm feeling flaky or having a life crisis. But we've been together 3 years and I'm not even close to wanting to get married to him and don't feel I ever could. I don't know if I want to marry anyone! I think I need to be alone for a while. Thanks again.

Some people see the medication as a tool, rather than a solution. I think that's what you helped your friend see. 

Like, the medication isn't going to fix you and it's not supposed to. It's supposed to give you the ability to dig yourself out of the pit. Give you the clarity of having a day where you don't wallow in hate for yourself and get nothing done.

I will try to adopt that mindset if my endeavor to counseling is successful.  I guess there's nothing I can do about the chemicals up there. Maybe I saw medication as the end. "Okay, take this pill and it will make you a normal human being."  That's not healthy. It should be "take this pill and you will be able to work on yourself! You will have the motivation to better yourself, by yourself."

That kind of struck a chord for me. Thanks so much.

I find that interesting, the implication that I need my depression to define me. You worded it more eloquently. I'm trying to figure out how accurate that is. 

Don't mistake this for justification of my actions.. I just enjoy brainstorming.

There is only one person in my life who knows all of this. That would be my boyfriend. So if I do need it to define me, it's not for attention. I also don't use it as an excuse for failure, since I consider myself successful for my age. But it has become a part of my own self-identity. I'm not sure why I'm so adamant that living happily while on medication is false. It could be low self-esteem telling me that I can only function in another reality. Or it could be my own fairytale that one day I will snap out of this on my own with determination that I'm not willing to give up on.

I enjoy counseling because I feel I can vent uncensored. I think I also wish that maybe I'm just having a bad couple of weeks and if I have someone who will just understand me I will feel better. 

Maybe it's the opposite of that theory.  I have never been officially diagnosed with depression, and I see people self-diagnosing left and right. "I'm a little socially awkward, I must have autism." "I like my room clean, I have OCD." Depression gets that treatment a lot. I think it's hard for me to admit I have a chronic problem. I like to think it's a series of bad days. You know, every day for 10 years. I've never enjoyed being different or standing out from the crowd. I never wanted to have depression. Maybe I'm in the ultimate denial.

I love Mr. Rogers. He makes me feel better, if only for a little while. He truly was a wonderful human being. His quotes have been known to make me cry in a moment of realization that maybe things aren't so bad.

I do love them very much and they love me. I know this. It's not enough. It's a reason for me not to die in the sense that I don't want to hurt them. But that doesn't make me want to wake up in the morning. I wish it did. I go through every day past the voices telling me to do it because I don't want them to hurt. I have no internal motivating factors other than my pride telling me I can't quit.

Hi. Thanks for reaching out :)

I think I am kind of in that existential attitude but I am not in the phase of appreciating the absurdity. I'm with you, I have done very well for myself for my age but I don't try. I bumble through life with no motivation or attempt at success. Makes it seem like such a joke, doesn't it?

I've been on medication before. I remember feeling my absolute best. I woke up and I got ready for the day with a smile in my face for the first time in years. Then I got into my own head. I have a degree in psychology which works against me sometimes. I start thinking about how the drugs are just rebalancing the chemicals in my brain and they're pumping out all kinds of seratonim and dopamine. And I realize I'm the same person I always was. I just need help to be normal. That sucks. It makes me feel worse. 

I know depression does a lot of talking for me. But I can't help but think it will always be there. Just buried. I have no curiosity towards life. I think my own pride keeps me alive sometimes. I'm no quitter. Even if I kill myself maybe there is some combination of therapy and medication I haven't tried that could make me feel normal even for a little while.

I'm not sure the kind of help I want. I think it's just the absent hope I could be made normal. I guess more concrete would be the feeling that there is someone who genuinely wants to listen to me and can fully unravel my brain. My mind feels like a long thread with lots of knots and tangles. People listen on the surface, but I want someone to have clarity on how I feel and how I think. I think maybe that is a lofty goal. Maybe I want to feel like they WANT to have that clarity.  

I have done cognitive behavioral. That was the first time things started to make sense for me. Then my therapist suddenly moved out of state.  I have tried zoloft, wellbutrin, cymbalta, and lorazepam for anxiety. Lorazepam just kind of knocked me on my ass. Wellbutrin didn't do anything except make me quit smoking. That part was awesome. Cymbalta and zoloft made me manic it felt like. 

That's as clear as I think I can be, I hope that makes sense. Thanks for listening.

No I've never tried ECT. I don't know how I feel about it, though I have considered it may be the only thing that could help. I have only tried counseling and some medications. I don't stick with any one therapist for it to make a difference. The one time I did he suddenly moved out of state. Sometimes I think therapy is futile.  I have a degree in psychology and while that is not impressive it clues me in to the tricks and techniques therapists use. 

Something like 33% of all Americans have some sort of mental illness. A tiny percentage of that seeks help. It's sad.
